# GDAL downsampling and windowed tile rendering

*Generated by Codex from the current plugin code and repository history.*

Make large rasters practical to georeference interactively in QGIS 4. Read
only the source area needed for the current view, at a resolution appropriate
for the render target.

## Current behavior

`load_raster_for_display()` calls `ReadAsArray()` for every band at full
resolution, then converts the arrays into a single `QImage`. The layer keeps
that image in memory, and both the main renderer and the drag preview paint it
at the current position, scale and rotation. Opening a large raster can
therefore require several full-image allocations even when the raster fits
in a small part of the canvas or only a corner is visible.

## Task

- Load raster metadata and original dimensions independently of display
  pixels. Use the original dimensions for layer extents, transform math,
  replacement-image validation and world-file export.
- Map the visible render area back into source pixel coordinates using the
  current transform. Clip reads to the raster bounds and account for rotation,
  unequal X/Y scale and the render target's pixel density. Skip pixel reads
  when the raster is outside the view.
- Use GDAL window reads at a display-appropriate resolution. Use suitable
  overviews when available and request downsampled buffers for rasters without
  overviews. At close zoom, read the visible area at up to native resolution.
- Render bounded tiles and reuse them across redraws where possible. Bound the
  memory used by the tile cache and discard cached data when the source
  changes. Handle cancelled renders and failed reads safely.
- Apply the approach to both the layer renderer and the drag preview. Keep
  tiles aligned under the same transform and preserve the existing band
  selection, color tables, alpha and nodata handling. Use a consistent
  display range for non-Byte data so neighboring tiles and zoom levels have
  consistent colors.
- Keep export independent of the viewport. World-file-only export should
  require source dimensions and georeferencing only. Image export should use
  the source at the resolution required by the existing export mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- A large raster opens and draws while zoomed out without allocating a
  full-resolution display image. Verify this with and without GDAL overviews.
- Zooming in resolves source detail. Panning limits reads to the relevant
  area and reuses cached tiles where possible. Rotation, scaling and the drag
  preview show no gaps or shifts at tile boundaries.
- Paletted rasters, transparency and non-Byte rasters render consistently
  across tile boundaries and zoom levels. Replacing a source does not display
  tiles from the previous source.
- Existing project transforms and world-file coordinates agree at all zoom
  levels. Image export produces the expected dimensions regardless of what is
  currently visible on the canvas.
